result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001: 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong. The grades are in `grades/0001-s1.json`, with feedback on every item.

| Item | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | You identified the loop as what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Wrong (M4) | The model outputs a tool request. The program runs the tool; the model doesn't open the booking system. |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit is the right safeguard when the agent repeats itself. |
| q4 | Wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls: 3 tool requests plus the final answer. You said 1, with the model running the tools itself. |
| q5 | Partial | You said the result goes back to the model, but not why: so the model can choose its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | Partial (M3) | You were right that the model picks from tool descriptions. You were wrong that it remembers earlier sessions by itself. |

**What to work on:** the model only writes text, such as a tool request. The program runs the tools and calls the model again for each step. Memory is something the program has to build and save, so it isn't automatic.

**Next step:** redo the laser cutter trace ("free at 3 pm, and do I need training?") and label each step "model call" or "program action". Then count the model calls. That also sets up the context and memory lesson.

I also added learning record `0003-who-runs-the-tools.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s2.json` is still ungraded; I can grade it next to see whether these two misconceptions have changed.
